newsitem.title: LATVIA: LATTELEKOM STATE STAKE SALE NOT BEFORE MAY '98.
newsitem.headline: LATTELEKOM STATE STAKE SALE NOT BEFORE MAY '98.

text.p: The sale of the state's stake in Lattelekom will not take place before May or June of 1998, the Latvian Privatisation Agency said on Wednesday.
It also said it hoped to turn the company into a public stock company this year from its current limited company status.
The state has a 51 percent stake in Lattelekom which has been earmarked for sell-off.

The LPA is currently taking over the administration of the state's stake from the transport ministry and has to audit the umbrella agreement between Tilts, the company's other ownder, the state and Lattelekom.
Tilts Communications consortium, formed by Britain's Cable & Wireless, Telecom Finland and the World Bank's International Finance Corporation, holds 49 percent in Lattelekom.
The audit was agreed as necessary by all sides following disputes over the shortening of Lattelekom's phone monopoly to 2003 from 2013.

The umbrella agreement, signed in 1994, gave Tilts monopoly status to recoup its investment and it has said it would be unable to continue its costly investment in Latvia's telephone system if its monopoloy period was cut short.
